Trauma Emergencies

⏱ Deep Dive
📚 Trauma / Critical Care

Your Progress

0% complete

Overview

This course walks trauma from mechanism to transfer of care. Focus is pattern recognition, prioritizing life threats, and making good decisions fast.

  • Use X-ABCDE as the spine of every trauma call.
  • Think “can kill in minutes” first, then everything else.
  • Decide early who needs trauma center and activate from the field.

Trauma Assessments

  • Primary survey: X-ABCDE with explicit exsanguination step.
  • Rapid trauma exam vs focused exam.
  • Trauma scores you actually use: RTS, GCS, Shock Index, triage tags.

Mechanism of Injury & Kinematics

  • Blunt vs penetrating patterns.
  • Vehicle speed, intrusion, ejection, restraint use.
  • Falls, crush, blast, and combined mechanisms.

Bleeding & Shock

  • Class I–IV shock with field clues instead of pure numbers.
  • External vs internal hemorrhage patterns.
  • Tourniquets, packing, junctional control, TXA timing.

Soft Tissue Trauma

  • Contusions, abrasions, lacs, avulsions, degloving.
  • When you care about cosmetic outcome vs function vs survival.
  • Burn overlap, open fractures, and infection risk.

Head, Face, and Neck Trauma

  • TBI recognition, herniation signs, and when to hyperventilate.
  • Airway threats from facial trauma and neck wounds.
  • C-spine decision rules in the trauma patient.

Spinal / Neurological Trauma

  • Spinal cord syndromes and what you can see prehospital.
  • Neuro checks that actually change your plan.
  • Immobilization vs spinal motion restriction in real life.

Chest Trauma

  • Open chest wounds, flail, tension pneumo, tamponade.
  • When to dart, when to seal, when to move.
  • ECG and hemodynamics in blunt cardiac injury.

Abdominal Trauma

  • Solid vs hollow organ injury patterns.
  • Kehr’s sign, Grey–Turner, Cullen, and what they tell you.
  • Why your patient can look “stable” and still be bleeding out.

Pelvic Trauma

  • Pelvic ring injuries and the hidden blood loss they carry.
  • Pelvic binders: when, how high, and how tight.
  • Red flags for urethral or bladder injury.

Orthopedic Trauma

  • Open vs closed fractures and dislocations.
  • Neurovascular checks before and after any manipulation.
  • Compartment and crush red flags that demand rapid transport.

Diamond of Death

  • Hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy, and hypocalcemia.
  • How each one feeds the others in trauma.
  • Field moves to slow that spiral.

Damage Control Resuscitation

  • Permissive hypotension until hemorrhage control.
  • Balanced resuscitation mindset instead of “wide open fluids.”
  • Move to knife and light, not endless tricks in the back of the truck.

This tab ties together shock, bleeding, hypothermia, and your resuscitation choices.
